name: apple celery salad
instructions:
Two variants. Both share the apple + celery base dressed with lemon juice + zest.

- VARIANT A — SIMPLE: apple, celery, lemon juice + zest, mint. That's it.
- VARIANT B — BUILT-UP / CELEBRATORY: adds fennel bulb, walnuts, almonds, olive oil. Mint can be swapped for black pepper + parmesan cheese.

=== SHARED PREP ===

- Finely dice the apple.
- Slice or dice the celery (a small dice for the simple version; a slightly larger cut for the built-up version reads nicer against the fennel).
- Dress with lemon juice + lemon zest (see notes — that's the whole vinaigrette; no vinegar).

=== VARIANT A — SIMPLE ===

INGREDIENTS:
- apples, finely diced
- celery, small dice
- lemon juice + zest
- fresh mint leaves, chiffonaded (fine cut, off stems)

PROCEDURE:
1. Combine apples + celery in a bowl.
2. Dress with lemon juice + zest.
3. Fold in chiffonaded mint just before serving.

=== VARIANT B — BUILT-UP / CELEBRATORY ===

INGREDIENTS:
- apples, finely diced
- celery, small-to-medium dice
- FENNEL BULB, thinly sliced or small dice
- lemon juice + zest
- olive oil
- WALNUTS (slivered or roughly chopped)
- ALMONDS (slivered)
- MINT (chiffonaded), OR — swap for — BLACK PEPPER + PARMESAN CHEESE

PROCEDURE:
1. Combine apples + celery + fennel bulb in a bowl.
2. Dress with lemon juice + zest + olive oil.
3. Scatter walnuts + almonds.
4. Finish with EITHER chiffonaded mint OR a generous grind of black pepper + shaved/grated parmesan. Not both — pick a direction.
notes:
=== VINAIGRETTE IS JUST LEMON — NO VINEGAR (BOTH VARIANTS) ===

Lemon juice + zest is acidic enough on its own — no additional vinegar needed. Unlike tangerine (too sweet to carry a salad acid by itself), lemon does the whole job.

=== VARIANT B — MINT OR BLACK PEPPER + PARMESAN (SWAP, NOT COMBINE) ===

The two finish options push variant B in different directions:
- MINT: brighter, greener finish. Same direction as variant A (mint is the default there).
- BLACK PEPPER + PARMESAN: warmer, more italian-antipasto register. The pepper's warmth and parmesan's salt-and-umami take the salad into a different, richer place.

Don't stack them — pick one. The two together compete rather than combine.

=== MINT PAIRS WITH APPLE AND LEMON ===

Chiffonaded fresh mint works beautifully across both variants. Mint pairs with the apple's sweetness and the lemon's tang — natural partners. Fold in just before serving so the leaves stay fresh. (Note this doesn't contradict the tangerine-mint-vinaigrette clash below: the issue there is tangerine's sweetness compounding with the apple, not the mint itself. Mint alone is welcome; mint-as-a-vehicle-for-tangerine is not.)

=== WHY TANGERINE MINT VINAIGRETTE CLASHES ===

Too sweet for this salad even with vinegar added. Apple is already bringing sweetness; you need a sharp acid here, not another sweet-acid layer.

=== HISTORICAL NOTE — RED ONIONS REMOVED ===

Earlier version of this recipe (when it was called apple fennel salad) had red onions as a primary. Removed — the user's landing is simpler. If you want an allium in variant B, sauté or pickle first (raw red onion is too aggressive against the apple/fennel/lemon balance); but the current recipe skips onion entirely.
